About

Praneeth Suresh

ML engineer and computer science and mathematics student at the National University of Singapore (double major, 2025–2028). I work on tools that make AI-assisted software development checkable, and I keep my study notes public.

Now

I maintain Beryl, a set of repository files and checks for working with coding agents, and I am researching, as CP3106 independent research at NUS, whether machine-readable repository policies with deterministic enforcement improve coding-agent outcomes over the same rules in prose. The study is in progress and has no results yet.

My reading interests are interpretability, model evaluation, and agent reliability; the research questions page lists what I am working on and what would change my mind.

Work you can inspect

  • Beryl — An installable set of repository files and scripts that tell coding agents how to work in a project and check that some of those rules were actually followed.
  • Notes — this site — The site you are reading: a static build that turns my Notion study notes into public, searchable pages while keeping math, code, and nested pages intact.
  • SIAP — Structure and Interpretation of Agentic Patterns: a book in progress that teaches agent systems by building interpreters for reasoning and tool-use loops.
  • AI Society Corpus — An interactive knowledge graph for NUS AI Society that links AI/ML study topics by prerequisites, shared tags, and backlinks.

I also write about research reading and projects and keep computer science notes.
